content.description:
AFTER dr-w14-s3-gauge-sees-a-wrong-name MERGES AND AFTER dr-w13-s6-publish-clock-first-caller MERGES. ROUND 2 — this slice does NOT build beside them. S3 rewrites deploy_ledger.ex's anchors and this slice's @agency repair lands in the same module; S6 owns router.ex's /v1/sites/:id/deployments region while this slice owns router.ex's barkparks/status region. Rebase on main after BOTH land, then re-derive the conflict set before touching anything.

Charter D202 + D208 + D223 + D224 (origin/main, wave 14).

WHAT THIS IS. PR #10129 ("the fleet verdict reads the deploy rate — deploys_failing and unmetered") is the LAST open PR of the wave-13 set and it is CONFLICTING against main. It is also the ONLY thing standing between the epic and a fleet deploy arm: `git grep -n deploy_rate origin/main` returns exactly TWO lines, both charter prose. merge_deploy_rate/2 does not exist on main. `git grep deploys_failing origin/main -- internal/` exits 1. `bp cloud status -o json` top-level keys are literally barkparks, buckets, count, ok — every row's detail is "", including Guerrilla, the box producing every deferral in this epic. There is no deploy arm anywhere in the CLI.

THE REBASE IS PROVEN AND ITS SHAPE IS RATIFIED. D202's mechanical prediction reproduced EXACTLY at L1: SIX conflicts, all Go/JSON — cloud/priv/static/__fixtures__/attention_order.json, internal/cli/cloud_status_cmd.go, internal/cli/cloud_status_cmd_test.go, internal/cli/testdata/attention_order_cases.json, internal/cloudclient/client.go, internal/semrole/semrole.go — and cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/deploy_ledger.ex + cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/web/router.ex AUTO-MERGE. All six resolve by UNION. semrole.go in particular KEEPS strained/filling/unreported: take-theirs would DELETE three landed rungs.

THE LADDER IS THIRTEEN RUNGS (charter D224). main has 11, the PR has 10, the union is 13:
1 removal_failed (danger x) · 2 failed (danger x) · 3 suspended (warn !) · 4 degraded (warn !) · 5 deploys_failing (warn !) · 6 strained (warn !) · 7 filling (warn !) · 8 unreported (warn ?) · 9 unmetered (warn ?) · 10 behind (info ^) · 11 removing (in-flight ~) · 12 provisioning (in-flight ~) · 13 ok (healthy *).
deploys_failing at 5 and unmetered tone=warn are D202 verbatim. unmetered at rank 9 is D224's ruling on two grounds: bucket contiguity is RESTORED (attention becomes the unbroken run 1-10; the PR broke it for the first time by parking unmetered at 9 between two in-flight rungs) and tone monotonicity is preserved (semrole.go's own comment makes non-monotone tone the forbidden outcome — a warn rung below `behind` (info) makes a less urgent rung shout louder). Setting the fixture tone to warn FORCES adding unmetered to semrole.go's warn case arm: statusRole (table.go:283) is a pure delegation to semrole.For, and TestAttentionVocabularyMatchesFixture asserts statusRole(state) == fixture tone. That OVERRIDES the PR author's stated reasoning ("an unmeasured box makes no claim, and this package never guesses a role") — say so in the PR body rather than let a reviewer discover it.

unreported and unmetered STAY SEPARATE RUNGS, and unreported makes the case stronger not weaker: unreported = `live && last_seen_at == ""` (a fact about the HEARTBEAT); unmetered = `sites > 0 && rate.pct == nil` (a fact about the DEPLOY SAMPLE). A box can beat perfectly and be unmetered forever (jarl: 55 terminal deploys, under min_sample 200). Collapsing them would make that box print "never reported", which is FALSE — the same error class as calling an UP box unavailable. THE PR's deployBox HELPER AND ITS THREE JSON FIXTURE ROWS CARRY NO last_seen_at, so post-rebase every one classifies `unreported` and FIVE TESTS FAIL. Adding last_seen_at is not cosmetic: without it the entire deploy-rung test file asserts nothing. State that in-source at the helper.

THE MERGE-INDUCED DEFECT YOU MUST FIX (charter D224). deploy_ledger.ex auto-merges CLEAN and is SEMANTICALLY BROKEN by it. main landed the 503 split (BOX_DEPLOY_DISABLED_503 / BOX_RUNNER_UNAVAILABLE_503) into @classes after #10129 branched; #10129's @agency map — the class->agency table box_caused is computed from — knows only the retired BOX_UNAVAILABLE_503. Git had no textual conflict to raise: one side added to a list, the other added a map. Result: classes/0 ++ not_attempted_classes/0 = 19, @agency keys = 17, and deploy_ledger_test.exs:1881 (`assert class in known, "#{class} has no agency — the map is not exhaustive"`) fails on BOTH new classes. Had that guard not existed, both would have fallen to :ambiguous, SHRINKING the box-caused numerator in D148's forbidden direction over precisely the 265-row feature_not_configured population. Fix: add both classes to @agency as :box (same family as the class they replaced), ~8 lines. This is the strongest available argument for the epic's own thesis, found inside the epic's own PR — put it in the PR body.

THE WINDOW MUST BE PINNED AND TESTED (charter D208). box_rates/3's OWN window handling IS tested on the PR branch (deploy_ledger_test.exs "the window is PINNED — rows outside the bound are not counted"). What has ZERO tests anywhere is the ROUTER'S CHOICE of window: router.ex ~:1899-1900 on the PR branch is `deploy_to = DateTime.utc_now()` / `deploy_from = DateTime.add(deploy_to, -24, :hour)` — two bare literals with no test reading them, while the module's own moduledoc (deploy_ledger.ex:74) forbids exactly this in writing ("every window is PINNED by an explicit inserted_at") and parse_window/2 refuses a floating window for the census route BY DESIGN. The control plane holds two windowing doctrines in one file and the fleet vital uses the forbidden one. DO NOT go add tests to box_rates/3 and call it done. The target is the router's choice, and the test must RED when -24 moves.

THE ARM CARRIES ITS AMPLIFICATION CAVEAT (charter D223). Do NOT build a provenance label — the axis is refuted (27 teams, 13 sites, exactly ONE team owns any site). Publish the ATTEMPT rate, which is the only unit that clears @min_sample 200 at 24h, bound to a caveat computed from the row set the arm already reads:
  "N of M build attempts failed between <from> and <to>. Those attempts carry only R distinct content revisions across S auto-publishing sites — A attempts per revision (Fx fan-out to sibling sites, Rx retry within a site) — so this is a rate of ATTEMPTS, not of publishes. Per revision it is P%, which we do not publish as a rate because R is below our 200-sample floor."
Measured over D209's pinned window: ATTEMPT 452/2,446 = 18.48%; CHAIN 125/653 = 19.14%; UNIQUE PUBLISH 16/163 = 9.82% and 163 REFUSES against min_sample 200. Amplification decomposes 3.64x retry x 4.01x fan-out = 14.60 against a measured 14.59. A caveat naming TENANCY ("demo churn", "customer vs platform") is FORBIDDEN — it would assert a distinction the teams table refutes. If the caveat cannot be computed honestly from the arm's own rows, ship the rate with an explicit population caveat rather than a rate implying a customer base that does not exist.

TWO TRAPS. (1) A name-filtered `go test -run 'Attention'` is FORBIDDEN as proof: it reports GREEN against a corrupted expected_order because the consumer is TestRankBarkparksFixture, which that filter does not match. Run the FULL package. The ladder has FOUR owners, not three: attentionRankOrder, attention_order.json, attention_order_cases.json AND its expected_order array. (2) The SPA ladder in cloud/priv/static/app.js is still NINE rungs and diverges further after this lands. It is D150-fenced to CCH — DO NOT touch it, but STATE the widening gap in the PR body rather than let it be discovered. It is provably harmless to this rebase: `grep -c attention_order cloud/priv/static/__app.test.mjs` = 0, so the node harness never reads the fixture.

BUILDER MECHANICS. Work in a worktree off origin/main. `git fetch origin pull/10129/head:pr10129` then rebase onto origin/main. Fresh worktrees have no cloud/deps: `cp -R /Volumes/SATECHI/github/barkpark/cloud/deps <worktree>/cloud/deps`, and run mix from <worktree>/cloud. Use CC=/usr/bin/clang everywhere — the bare `cc` is a Claude wrapper and cgo dies with "unknown option '-E'".

FILE FENCE. You own the six conflict files plus deploy_ledger.ex's @agency, router.ex's barkparks/status region (~1893-1905) ONLY, and deploy_ledger_test.exs. Do NOT touch router.ex's /v1/sites/:id/deployments handler, do NOT touch internal/cli/cloud_site_cmd*.go (wave-14 S1), and do NOT touch cloud/priv/static/app.js.

NOT IN SCOPE, deliberately: raising min_sample; a WAITING alert; the SPA ladder; re-tiering any route's auth. registry.ex is NOT in the change set and has no vitals surface (`git grep -n vitals origin/main -- cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/registry.ex` returns zero) — do not go looking for one. There is no internal/agent/report.go work in this slice.

A fleet rate over a floating window, with no caveat naming its 14.6x amplification, is quotable dishonestly.
The router's window has never had a test, and the merge-induced @agency defect is caught only by a property assertion.
Spans internal/cli, internal/semrole, internal/cloudclient and the cloud deploy ledger.
